question: Should OpenClaw sponsor official FreeBSD support, and if so should it start as experimental/community support or Tier 1 release support?
rationale: The request spans support tier, package publication, installer/update behavior, service management, CI, docs, and release ownership, which automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Define experimental FreeBSD scope first
options.body: Approve a staged community or experimental plan that names package ownership, install/update path, service manager, docs, and smoke-proof expectations before any official support claim is advertised.

options.title: Promote FreeBSD to Tier 1
options.body: Accept ongoing FreeBSD release ownership and split the work into tracked tasks for ports/pkg publication, installer behavior, service management, CI, docs, and release validation.

options.title: Decline official FreeBSD support
options.body: Keep FreeBSD as community/source/npm use only and close the support-tier request after documenting that policy.

recommendation.title: Define experimental FreeBSD scope first
recommendation.body: Approve a staged community or experimental plan that names package ownership, install/update path, service manager, docs, and smoke-proof expectations before any official support claim is advertised.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision affects official platform/support tier and release ownership, and CONTRIBUTING.md identifies steipete as the project lead.
